entries.meaning: A finite, definite and effective procedure with specified inputs and at least one output; correctness and efficiency are separate requirements.
entries.citationQuote: Definitions and characteristics of an algorithm; examples

entries.meaning: f(n) is O(g(n)) when some constant c and threshold n0 make f(n) at most c·g(n) for every larger n.
entries.citationQuote: Asymptotic notations: order (O), Omega, Theta, with examples
entries.formula: f(n) = O(g(n)) if there exist c > 0 and n0 such that f(n) <= c*g(n) for all n >= n0

entries.meaning: On a sorted random-access array, binary search halves the interval; for n ≥ 1 the worst case uses at most floor(log2(n))+1 midpoint probes. Iteration needs O(1) auxiliary space; recursion O(log n).
entries.citationQuote: Best, average and worst-case complexity of linear and binary search

entries.meaning: Divide an instance, solve smaller instances and combine; dynamic programming instead reuses overlapping states. The method alone does not determine running time.
entries.citationQuote: Programming models: divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming

entries.meaning: A sort preserves the relative order of equal-key records. Merge must take left on equality and LSD Radix needs stable digit passes; Quick and ordinary Selection/Heap are unstable.
Different keys can share a home slot. Chaining keeps lists; open addressing probes other slots. Expected constant time requires controlled load/distribution; probing deletion needs tombstones.
entries.citationQuote: Hashing, hash tables, hash functions, collision and collision resolution

entries.meaning: For a connected, weighted undirected graph, a spanning tree of minimum total edge weight; it includes all vertices, has V−1 edges and no cycle. Prim grows one tree; Kruskal merges components using Union-Find.
entries.citationQuote: Minimum spanning tree: Prim's algorithm, Kruskal's algorithm

entries.meaning: Dijkstra requires non-negative edges; Bellman–Ford permits negative edges and detects reachable negative cycles; Floyd–Warshall computes all pairs and detects negative cycles by a negative diagonal.
